summary: Implement the stateless provider-neutral MCP application boundary with identity-derived tenancy, permission-filtered discovery, re-authorization, fail-closed audit and a Task-017 approval-only sensitive price-change request tool.

impacts.evidence: MCP identity contains a canonical tenancy.Scope derived by a trusted resolver. Tool schemas do not accept organization/workspace selectors and all canonical read/approval ports receive only identity scope.

Tool boundary-audit summaries retain only bounded tool/authorized-phase/argument digest metadata. Secret-shaped price-change reasons are rejected and raw tool/provider payloads are not copied into audit evidence.
A new additive MCP developer surface is introduced at POST /mcp. Existing REST/OpenAPI routes and schemas are unchanged.
MCP introduces no new event type. Sensitive requests reuse Task-017 governance.approval.requested.v1 transactional outbox evidence.
Connector SDK v1 and provider interfaces are unchanged. MCP calls provider-neutral search/legal-party/approval ports and never imports connector implementations.
Task 018 adds no storage schema. Audit and approval persistence reuse Tasks 003 and 017.

Origin/protocol/header validation happens before tool execution; discovery is authorization-filtered; direct calls are re-authorized; runtime composition denies identity by default; no secrets/raw DB are exposed.

commerce.price.change.request is write_sensitive and can only create a Task-017 approval request for pricing.price.updated; it never calls the pricing update repository directly and fails closed without matching policy.

Every authorized MCP call must append Task-003 audit evidence with identity tenant/actor, canonical risk and SHA-256 argument digest. Audit failure prevents tool execution; approval creation additionally records Task-017 atomic outcome audit/outbox evidence.

The price request uses a caller-generated canonical UUIDv7/ULID as the durable approval request id, replays the same request across retries/policy changes, rejects key reuse for a different intent, and SHA-256-binds exact price/version/currency/minor-units/reason. Direct downstream execution remains outside Task 018 and keeps its normal optimistic/idempotency boundary.
MCP performs no webhook or arbitrary network egress. Canonical providers own any later external operations.
The MCP process exposes stable structured startup/diagnostic events and normalized protocol/tool error classes without logging untrusted request details.
The change is migration-free and can be rolled back by removing/disabling the MCP process. Fail-closed default identity wiring prevents accidental anonymous service exposure during rollout.

Tests cover current protocol discovery, tenant isolation, permission-filtered discovery, direct-call denial, Origin/header mismatch, audit failure, Task-017 approval-only mutation request, intent binding and secret-shaped reason rejection.
